entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 74
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 12267 of 2023

Applicant :- Darshan
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Vinay Kumar Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Satyendra Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Vinay Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Satyendra Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the informant and Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State.
2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release her on bail in Case Crime No.859 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304-B and 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Loni, District Ghaziabad during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the daughter of the informant was performed with the son of applicant on 18.2.2018 and after marriage his daughter was being tortured by applicant and his family members including the husband of the deceased for want of dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- and a Honda City Car.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 2.6.2022 accused persons informed the informant that after consuming poison his daughter committed suicide.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation against the applicant is totally false and baseless and applicant is not having any concerned with the family affairs of his son and he neither tortured the deceased nor he ever demanded any dowry and only being father-in-law of the Darshan vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92444669/
1 deceased, he was implicated in the present matter by the informant.

He further submits that no specific allegation has been made against the applicant either in the FIR or in the statement of witnesses and on the basis of general allegation applicant along with the husband of the deceased and other family members made accused in the present matter.

5. He further submits that deceased was having pregnancy of about 8 months but her pregnancy was unfortunately terminated and thereafter she faced number of complications and only due to this complication she died and applicant and his family members immediately rushed the deceased to the Hospital where Doctor declared her dead and immediately thereafter informant was informed by applicant and this fact has been admitted by the informant in the FIR itself.

He further submits that after receiving information informant arrived at the house of applicant and with his consent cremation was done and he participated in the funeral of his daughter and after about two weeks, he moved application under Section 15(3) Cr.P.C. and on his application FIR of the present case was lodged.

6. He further submits that co-accused Kamlesh, the mother-in-law of the deceased, has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 19.4.2023 passed in Criminal Misc.Bail Application No.12222 of 2023 and, therefore, applicant may also be released on bail.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA and the learned counsel for the informant although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that co-accused Kamelsh, mother-in-law of deceased has been granted bail by this Court.

8. Learned counsel for the informant, however, submitted that mother-in-law was the lady but being head of the family applicant is having more responsibility and without informing the informant dead body of the deceased was cremated and, therefore, being father-in-law the case of applicant is distinguishable from the case of mother-in-law and being head of the family applicant should not be released on bail.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. It is the case in which it appears that FIR of the present case was lodged through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was also filed after about two weeks and further although the dead body of the deceased was disposed of but in the FIR it has been admitted by the informant that he received information from accused side about the death of his daughter.
11. Further, the mother-in-law of the deceased has already been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 19.4.2023 and case of applicant, who is the father-in-law cannot be distinguished from mother-in-law at this stage.
12.
Therefore, from the discussions made above, in my view,applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Darshan vs State Of U.P. on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92444669/
2
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant-Darshan be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
( i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
